Prune a transition tree to the contexts that change the prediction

Source: R/prune.R
prune_tree.Rd

prune_tree() removes the contexts of a fitted tree that predict the next state no differently from their shorter suffix, so that the long contexts that remain are those in which the additional history changes the prediction. This is the principle behind the learning of prediction suffix trees (Ron, Singer & Tishby, 1996) and the context algorithm for variable-length Markov chains (Bühlmann & Wyner, 1999). A fitted tree holds every context that occurs often enough, and many such contexts add parameters without adding information about what comes next.

It compares each leaf with its parent, the context one state shorter, and removes the leaf when the comparison does not pass the chosen criterion; leaves exposed by a removal are tested in turn until no leaf can be removed. The root is never removed. With "G2" a leaf is kept when the likelihood-ratio statistic of its counts against the parent's distribution exceeds the chi-square critical value at alpha with \(k - 1\) degrees of freedom (\(k\) states); each leaf is tested separately, without correction for multiple tests. With "KL" a leaf is kept when its Kullback-Leibler divergence from the parent, in nats, exceeds threshold. With "AIC" and "BIC" a leaf is kept when its log-likelihood, penalized by \(2(k - 1)\) or \(\log(n)(k - 1)\) (\(n\) the leaf's count), is better than that of the parent's prediction (Akaike, 1974; Schwarz, 1978). The probabilities of the contexts that remain are not changed. It returns a tree of the same class with fewer contexts.

To see how strongly each criterion prunes a tree, use compare_pruning(); to choose between pruned and unpruned trees on held-out data, use tune_tree(); to draw the "G2" decision along the suffix chain of one pathway, use plot_pruning(). The divergence column of tree_pathways() is in bits, whereas the "KL" threshold is in nats; divide a threshold in nats by log(2) to read it in bits.

Usage

prune_tree(
  tree,
  criterion = c("G2", "KL", "AIC", "BIC"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  threshold = 0.005
)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object, or a transitiontrees_group, whose trees are each pruned.

criterion

"G2" (default), "KL", "AIC" or "BIC".

alpha

Significance level for "G2", in (0, 1). Default 0.05.

threshold

Minimum divergence in nats for "KL". Default 0.005.

Value

An object of the same class as tree, with fewer contexts. A pruned tree prints [pruned] and the criterion in its header, and n_nodes() gives its size.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree, alpha is not a single number in (0, 1), or threshold is not a single non-negative number.

References

Akaike, H. (1974). A new look at the statistical model identification. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, 19(6), 716-723. doi:10.1109/TAC.1974.1100705

Bühlmann, P., & Wyner, A. J. (1999). Variable length Markov chains. The Annals of Statistics, 27(2), 480-513. doi:10.1214/aos/1018031204

Ron, D., Singer, Y., & Tishby, N. (1996). The power of amnesia: Learning probabilistic automata with variable memory length. Machine Learning, 25(2-3), 117-149. doi:10.1023/A:1026490906255

Schwarz, G. (1978). Estimating the dimension of a model. The Annals of Statistics, 6(2), 461-464. doi:10.1214/aos/1176344136

See also

compare_pruning(), plot_pruning(), tune_tree(), context_tree().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 4)
prune_tree(tree, criterion = "G2", alpha = 0.05)
#> <transitiontrees>  25 nodes, depth <= 4, 3 states  [pruned]
#>   alphabet : Active, Average, Disengaged
#>   fit on   : 136 sequences, 1870 observations
